MID-CYCLE MANUAL RUN: judgment written 2026-08-26, five calendar days after the 2026-08-21 close this file reads. Two of the five sessions in the week window (Mon 08-24, Tue 08-25) had already traded. The three catalysts that dominate the window -- July core PCE and NVDA earnings (both 08-26), and the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote (08-28) -- were all still ahead, and the pinned research snapshot (2026-08-24) carries no post-08-21 outcomes. The week horizon is still not a clean ex-ante forecast and must not be graded as one.

day.unavailable: The day horizon needs daily bars; the upstream feed commits Friday closes only.

why: Archetype 1 has Materials at +19.4 pct absolute, -11.9 pts excess -- a structural laggard in steady mid-cycle expansions (The Full Regime-Sector Matrix).

The bid is a narrative without demand data behind it: copper ~$4.20/lb with the gold/copper ratio at historic extremes, boosted by Chinese stimulus chatter rather than orders. Called 'speculative value' -- cheap on book, requiring a China story that may not arrive (wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433; wiki/materials.md@4b81bf6f).
risks: Two of the three extreme-move flags in this run are Materials names: NEM +41.2 pct and MP +45.4 pct over four weeks. Both are retained, not dropped, per the extreme-move gate, but a basket carrying two 40-plus pct moves is being driven by idiosyncratic stories (panel metrics, this file).

why: The panel has Materials +9.80 pts vs SPY on the month, well ahead of the archetype-1 prior, but 60.0 breadth on both horizons says the move is not broad (panel metrics, this file).

The XLE/XLB correlation spiked to ~0.80 this week as commodity beta became the dominant factor, so a large part of the Materials signal is the same trade as the Energy signal rather than an independent one (wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433).
risks: If the geopolitical premium in crude unwinds, the commodity-beta correlation that is currently lifting Materials reverses with it (wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433).
